competitorObservation.conclusion: Catalog count alone is not parity. Clervo must preserve exact identity, qualify every listed route, expose positive customer prices, and add production supply for search, RPC, data, storage, and payments rather than publish unavailable models.

candidates.starterBasis: 210 million compute units per 30 days on the authenticated free tier; public endpoints are less reliable
candidates.reason: The rotated key works across all 13 selected networks and closes the Fantom technical gap, but observed custom limits affected Base, BSC, and Optimism. The general license is non-transferable and non-sublicensable and does not expressly permit selling raw RPC access.
candidates.ownerAction: Obtain written permission for Clervo's paid customer-facing RPC gateway or use an expressly compatible replacement.

candidates.starterBasis: USD 5 recurring monthly credit, equivalent to 1,000 Search calls at USD 5 per 1,000, with 50 QPS capacity
candidates.reason: The dedicated key passed all five fixed-corpus checks with every official host ranked first and 189 ms p95. It is the best primary behind a provider-neutral normalized adapter, with the independently qualified existing source retained as fallback.

candidates.starterBasis: existing account; 10 GB storage, 1 million Class A, 10 million Class B monthly free allocation, zero egress charge
candidates.reason: The dedicated private bucket and single-bucket credential passed write, integrity-checked read, delete, and absence verification. The bounded adapter is ready for preview; a durable global usage ledger remains required before horizontal production scaling.

candidates.starterBasis: advertised 50 million compute units monthly free tier
candidates.reason: The 50 million CU free tier is technically attractive, but the current general terms limit Website and API use to personal non-commercial use and do not grant raw RPC resale rights, so another account would not close the customer-supply gap.

candidates.starterBasis: Alchemy 30M CU/month; Quicknode 10M credits/month; Chainstack 3M requests/month; Infura 3M credits/day; Ankr 200M credits/month; GetBlock self-serve access
candidates.reason: Every reviewed current agreement prohibits resale, sublicensing, third-party-benefit access, competitive gateway use, or commercial exploitation without written permission. Opening six more free accounts would add credentials but no launch-safe customer supply.

candidates.starterBasis: 100,000 credits/day, 5 RPS, all supported EVM chains, and no credit card
candidates.reason: This is the clear zero-cash technical winner for normalized EVM wallet, token, and transaction data: one multichain key, intended dapp/wallet/agent use, large recurring allowance, and a bounded adapter. Six credentialed normalized checks passed across Ethereum and Base. Raw API and RPC resale are excluded.
Useful fallback but unnecessary account and adapter complexity while the existing object-storage account can be repaired.
The trial explicitly excludes production and the first commercial production plan is not compatible with zero owner cash.

candidates.starterBasis: 10 million billing units recurring monthly, but a payment method is required and overage is billable
candidates.reason: The existing account is valuable later, but Node traffic remains disabled until a hard application guard and verified billing cap prevent owner-cash overage.

FLUX Schnell and open-license DreamShaper each passed only 1/5 independent composition cases. The stronger newer BFL routes are positively priced but their current API terms expressly prohibit exposing the models behind a third-party integration API. No owned edge image route is an honest sale fallback.

candidates.starterBasis: 25 one-time credits: about eight Core, six Turbo, or three Ultra successful images
candidates.reason: The official API permits commercial outputs and is a strong paid replacement candidate, but its one-time starter allowance cannot back meaningful launch traffic. Opening the account now would add an owner credential and benchmark-only supply, not resilient zero-owner-cash capacity.

candidates.starterBasis: USD 0.10 recurring monthly routed-inference credit for a free user
candidates.reason: The recurring credit is useful for experimentation but too small for a reliable paid customer route, and the routed multi-provider layer adds no advantage over the exact qualified suppliers already owned.

candidates.starterBasis: no-card free plan advertising up to 100 million monthly compute units and 300 CUPS
candidates.reason: The current terms target developer and dapp use and do not show an express resale prohibition, but they also do not expressly authorize a paid raw-RPC gateway. Coverage is narrower than the already qualified dedicated source, so a new account does not remove the written-permission blocker.
The free tier explicitly auto-routes around unavailable models, which cannot satisfy Clervo exact-model identity, and depending on the direct competitor is not an independent supply foundation.
No sufficiently clear primary commercial terms, supplier provenance, exact-identity guarantee, or production SLA was proven.

The phrase did not resolve to one verifiable zero-cash production API: Omni-Dreams is a 2B-parameter research model, Tokenator advertises a paid 2B-token bundle with opaque upstreams, and the Google Omni aggregator requires a paid plan. None improves the launch supply safely.
